svg.title: A peaked next-token distribution has lower entropy than an even one
svg.desc: Two toy distributions over tokens A, B, and C. Here H denotes Shannon entropy, ln denotes the natural logarithm, and a nat is the natural-logarithm unit of information. Exponentiating H gives the equivalent number of equally likely token choices. On the left, probabilities 0.90, 0.05, and 0.05 give entropy H about 0.394 nats, equivalent to about 1.48 equally likely choices. On the right, each token has probability one third, so the entropy is the natural logarithm of 3 (ln 3), about 1.099 nats, equivalent to 3 equally likely choices. Bar length is probability.
svg.text: Entropy measures how the probability is spread
Bar length is probability. The tokens are the same. Only the probabilities change.
Most of the probability is on A.
B and C are short bars, not missing.
Each token is an equal choice.
The three bars have the same length.
A certain prediction has entropy 0. Spreading the same probability raises it. The names A, B, and C do not.
